before.abstract_zh: 对复杂公允价值估计的审计涉及评价和质疑客户的关键假设。审计师通常缺乏执行这项工作所需的专业知识，因此，他们常常聘请估值专家来执行这项审计工作。然而，估值专家主要从事咨询工作，可能不会对其审计工作给予足够的谨慎。我们考察估值专家对审计工作的心理所有权以及审计师对该工作的侵犯是否会影响专家的判断质量。通过对执业估值专家进行的一项调查和一项实验，我们发现，较高的心理所有权会改善专家的证据评价和判断，但仅在审计师不以侵犯其工作的方式行事时如此。当审计师行为具有侵入性时，专家较高心理所有权带来的益处便消失。我们的发现表明，审计质量不仅取决于专家行为，还取决于审计师与专家的互动。我们的研究为审计事务所如何组织审计工作以及管理审计师与估值专家之间的内部工作关系提供了实践指导。

 Audits of complex fair value estimates involve evaluating and challenging key client assumptions. Auditors generally lack the necessary expertise to perform this work, and thus, they often engage valuation specialists to perform this audit work. However, valuation specialists primarily perform advisory work and may not put enough care into their audit work. We examine whether valuation specialists' psychological ownership of audit work and auditors' infringement on that work affect specialists' judgment quality. Using a survey and an experiment with practicing valuation specialists, we find that higher psychological ownership improves specialists' evidence evaluation and judgments, but only when auditors do not behave intrusively by infringing on their work. When auditors behave intrusively, the benefits of specialists' higher psychological ownership disappear. Our findings show that audit quality depends not only on specialist behavior but also on auditor interactions with specialists. Our study offers practical guidance to audit firms on how to organize audit work and manage internal working relationships between auditors and valuation specialists.

blocks.text: Specialists' Evidence Evaluation and Judgments in Audits

Audits of complex fair value estimates involve evaluating and challenging key client assumptions. Auditors generally lack the necessary expertise to perform this work, and thus, they often engage valuation specialists to perform this audit work. However, valuation specialists primarily perform advisory work and may not put enough care into their audit work. We examine whether valuation specialists' psychological ownership of audit work and auditors' infringement on that work affect specialists' judgment quality. Using a survey and an experiment with practicing valuation specialists, we find that higher psychological ownership improves specialists' evidence evaluation and judgments, but only when auditors do not behave intrusively by infringing on their work. When auditors behave intrusively, the benefits of specialists' higher psychological ownership disappear. Our findings show that audit quality depends not only on specialist behavior but also on auditor interactions with specialists. Our study offers practical guidance to audit firms on how to organize audit work and manage internal working relationships between auditors and valuation specialists.

before.abstract_zh: 对复杂公允价值估计的审计涉及评价和质疑客户的关键假设。审计师通常缺乏执行这项工作所需的专业知识，因此，他们常常聘请估值专家来执行这项审计工作。然而，估值专家主要从事咨询工作，可能不会对其审计工作给予足够的谨慎。我们考察估值专家对审计工作的心理所有权以及审计师对该工作的侵犯是否会影响专家的判断质量。通过对执业估值专家进行的一项调查和一项实验，我们发现，较高的心理所有权会改善专家的证据评价和判断，但仅在审计师不以侵犯其工作的方式行事时如此。当审计师行为具有侵入性时，专家较高心理所有权带来的益处便消失。我们的发现表明，审计质量不仅取决于专家行为，还取决于审计师与专家的互动。我们的研究为审计事务所如何组织审计工作以及管理审计师与估值专家之间的内部工作关系提供了实践指导。

blocks.text: Specialists' Evidence Evaluation and Judgments in Audits

Audits of complex fair value estimates involve evaluating and challenging key client assumptions. Auditors generally lack the necessary expertise to perform this work, and thus, they often engage valuation specialists to perform this audit work. However, valuation specialists primarily perform advisory work and may not put enough care into their audit work. We examine whether valuation specialists' psychological ownership of audit work and auditors' infringement on that work affect specialists' judgment quality. Using a survey and an experiment with practicing valuation specialists, we find that higher psychological ownership improves specialists' evidence evaluation and judgments, but only when auditors do not behave intrusively by infringing on their work. When auditors behave intrusively, the benefits of specialists' higher psychological ownership disappear. Our findings show that audit quality depends not only on specialist behavior but also on auditor interactions with specialists. Our study offers practical guidance to audit firms on how to organize audit work and manage internal working relationships between auditors and valuation specialists.

 Les audits portant sur des estimations complexes de la juste valeur requièrent une évaluation et une remise en question des principales hypothèses formulées par le client. En règle générale, les auditeurs ne possèdent pas l'expertise nécessaire pour accomplir ces tâches et, de ce fait, ils les confient souvent à des spécialistes en évaluation. Cependant, ceux-ci offrent principalement des services de consultation et pourraient ne pas aborder les mandats d'audit avec la même rigueur. Nous vérifions si le sentiment d'appropriation psychologique qu'éprouvent les spécialistes à l'égard de leur travail d'audit, ainsi que l'ingérence des auditeurs dans ce travail, influence la qualité des jugements des spécialistes. À l'aide d'un sondage et d'une expérience réalisés auprès de spécialistes en évaluation, nous établissons que le fait d'éprouver un fort sentiment d'appropriation psychologique améliore l'évaluation des éléments de preuve et la qualité des jugements chez les spécialistes, mais uniquement lorsque les auditeurs ne se comportent pas de manière intrusive en empiétant sur leur travail, sinon les avantages associés à un fort sentiment d'appropriation psychologique chez les spécialistes disparaissent. Nos résultats montrent que la qualité d'un audit repose non seulement sur le comportement des spécialistes, mais également sur la qualité des interactions entre auditeurs et spécialistes. Notre étude fournit aux cabinets d'audit des orientations pratiques sur la façon d'organiser les travaux d'audit et de gérer les relations de travail internes entre les auditeurs et les spécialistes en évaluation.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 1 Introduction
 
 While valuation specialists employed by public accounting firms primarily prepare valuations for advisory clients, they also critically assist audit teams with testing the complex and subjective valuations reported in financial statements for most audits (Zimmerman et al. 2023). Concerns exist about audit teams' heavy reliance on valuation and other specialists, whose first priority is their advisory work (e.g., PCAOB 2015; Anantharaman 2017; Barr-Pulliam et al. 2023). Many concerns coalesce around the extent of specialists' ownership of various aspects of the audit. Auditors voice concerns about specialists' lack of care for their audit work, while specialists voice concerns about auditor interference with their audit work (Bauer and Estep 2019; Griffith 2020).
 
 We conduct a survey and experiment with practicing valuation specialists to investigate specialists' ownership of their audit work and its effects on their evidence evaluation and judgments. The survey provides insight into valuation specialists' psychological ownership over audit work. Psychological ownership is a feeling that something is your own (Pierce et al. 2001, 2004). The experiment examines whether increasing specialists' psychological ownership over audit work improves their evidence evaluation and judgments and whether auditor infringement that threatens specialists' ownership of this work interferes with psychological ownership and its benefits. Infringement arises when actions taken by others are perceived to threaten, intrude on, and lay claim to another's target of ownership (Brown 2009; Kirk et al. 2018; Micu and Ashley 2022).
 
 Our survey finds that valuation specialists' feelings of ownership vary across audit engagements, as do the factors that influence these feelings. Practicing specialists feel greater ownership when they have the opportunity to engage in their audit work and when their work is valued, and the specific factors they cite are consistent with theory. The survey informs our experiment by (1) affirming the validity of psychological ownership and the factors that affect it in the auditor–specialist context and (2) documenting both lower specialist ownership that could be increased and higher specialist ownership that could be threatened by auditor infringement.
 
 Our experiment investigates the joint influence of specialists' psychological ownership and auditor infringement on specialists' audit work. We expect psychological ownership to improve specialists' evidence evaluation and judgments because it is positively associated with responsibility and motivation (Vandewalle et al. 1995; Jussila et al. 2015), which are precursors to the type of thinking needed to effectively perform specialists' tasks, such as integrating evidence with preexisting knowledge and identifying conflicting information (Griffith et al. 2016; Kadous and Zhou 2019). Infringing on a target of ownership, however, can lead to behavior such as disengagement from the target (Brown et al. 2005; Kirk et al. 2018). We expect infringement will stifle the beneficial effects of higher ownership. We predict specialists with higher ownership who do not face infringement will evaluate evidence more effectively and make more appropriate judgments than both specialists with lower ownership and specialists who face infringement.

 Les audits portant sur des estimations complexes de la juste valeur requièrent une évaluation et une remise en question des principales hypothèses formulées par le client. En règle générale, les auditeurs ne possèdent pas l'expertise nécessaire pour accomplir ces tâches et, de ce fait, ils les confient souvent à des spécialistes en évaluation. Cependant, ceux-ci offrent principalement des services de consultation et pourraient ne pas aborder les mandats d'audit avec la même rigueur. Nous vérifions si le sentiment d'appropriation psychologique qu'éprouvent les spécialistes à l'égard de leur travail d'audit, ainsi que l'ingérence des auditeurs dans ce travail, influence la qualité des jugements des spécialistes. À l'aide d'un sondage et d'une expérience réalisés auprès de spécialistes en évaluation, nous établissons que le fait d'éprouver un fort sentiment d'appropriation psychologique améliore l'évaluation des éléments de preuve et la qualité des jugements chez les spécialistes, mais uniquement lorsque les auditeurs ne se comportent pas de manière intrusive en empiétant sur leur travail, sinon les avantages associés à un fort sentiment d'appropriation psychologique chez les spécialistes disparaissent. Nos résultats montrent que la qualité d'un audit repose non seulement sur le comportement des spécialistes, mais également sur la qualité des interactions entre auditeurs et spécialistes. Notre étude fournit aux cabinets d'audit des orientations pratiques sur la façon d'organiser les travaux d'audit et de gérer les relations de travail internes entre les auditeurs et les spécialistes en évaluation.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 1 Introduction
 
 While valuation specialists employed by public accounting firms primarily prepare valuations for advisory clients, they also critically assist audit teams with testing the complex and subjective valuations reported in financial statements for most audits (Zimmerman et al. 2023). Concerns exist about audit teams' heavy reliance on valuation and other specialists, whose first priority is their advisory work (e.g., PCAOB 2015; Anantharaman 2017; Barr-Pulliam et al. 2023). Many concerns coalesce around the extent of specialists' ownership of various aspects of the audit. Auditors voice concerns about specialists' lack of care for their audit work, while specialists voice concerns about auditor interference with their audit work (Bauer and Estep 2019; Griffith 2020).
 
 We conduct a survey and experiment with practicing valuation specialists to investigate specialists' ownership of their audit work and its effects on their evidence evaluation and judgments. The survey provides insight into valuation specialists' psychological ownership over audit work. Psychological ownership is a feeling that something is your own (Pierce et al. 2001, 2004). The experiment examines whether increasing specialists' psychological ownership over audit work improves their evidence evaluation and judgments and whether auditor infringement that threatens specialists' ownership of this work interferes with psychological ownership and its benefits. Infringement arises when actions taken by others are perceived to threaten, intrude on, and lay claim to another's target of ownership (Brown 2009; Kirk et al. 2018; Micu and Ashley 2022).
 
 Our survey finds that valuation specialists' feelings of ownership vary across audit engagements, as do the factors that influence these feelings. Practicing specialists feel greater ownership when they have the opportunity to engage in their audit work and when their work is valued, and the specific factors they cite are consistent with theory. The survey informs our experiment by (1) affirming the validity of psychological ownership and the factors that affect it in the auditor–specialist context and (2) documenting both lower specialist ownership that could be increased and higher specialist ownership that could be threatened by auditor infringement.
 
 Our experiment investigates the joint influence of specialists' psychological ownership and auditor infringement on specialists' audit work. We expect psychological ownership to improve specialists' evidence evaluation and judgments because it is positively associated with responsibility and motivation (Vandewalle et al. 1995; Jussila et al. 2015), which are precursors to the type of thinking needed to effectively perform specialists' tasks, such as integrating evidence with preexisting knowledge and identifying conflicting information (Griffith et al. 2016; Kadous and Zhou 2019). Infringing on a target of ownership, however, can lead to behavior such as disengagement from the target (Brown et al. 2005; Kirk et al. 2018). We expect infringement will stifle the beneficial effects of higher ownership. We predict specialists with higher ownership who do not face infringement will evaluate evidence more effectively and make more appropriate judgments than both specialists with lower ownership and specialists who face infringement.
